title: Breaking a big job into small steps
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: How do I start a big job?
Tidying my room is too much
How can I break a task into steps?

figure.verdict: Small steps make a big job easy

explain.say: Have you ever looked at a messy room and thought, That is too much? Look at the board. On the left is one big job. On the right, the same job, cut into small steps.

explain.say: See the left side? Tidy my whole room. It feels huge, so it is hard to start. That is not your fault. Big jobs feel heavy for everyone. Does a big job ever make you want to give up?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Small steps make a big job easy

explain.say: Now look at the right side. Toys in the box. Books on the shelf. Clothes in the basket. Each step is small and easy. You do one, then the next. Which step would you do first?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Small steps make a big job easy

explain.say: Here is the list. See the first step glow? Only toys first. Do not think about books or clothes yet. Just toys. When it is done, tick it. Can you feel how much lighter that is?

steps.label: Rubbish in bin
steps.ask: How do I split my own big job?

explain.say: Last one, rubbish in the bin, and the whole room is tidy! You did a big job, one small step at a time. Here is a challenge. Pick a big job, and tell a grown-up its three small steps.

steps.label: Rubbish in bin
steps.ask: How do I split my own big job?

faq.a: A small step is easy to start. Each tick feels good, and that gives you energy for the next step.
asks: Tell me about Toys in the box

faq.q: How do I split my own big job?
faq.a: Ask yourself, What is the very first thing I do? Write or draw it. Then ask, What comes next? Keep going until the job is done.
asks: Tell me about Rubbish in bin

faq.q: What if a step still feels too big?
faq.a: Cut it again. Instead of all the toys, try just the cars. Any step can be made smaller.

faq.q: Can someone help me make the steps?
faq.a: Yes. You can say, Can you help me break this up, please? A grown-up you trust can help you write the list.

faq.q: Does this work for school work too?
faq.a: Yes. A story can be: plan, start, middle, end, check. A project can be split the same way.
asks: Can I use this for homework?

facts: Breaking a task into small steps is sometimes called chunking.
Ticking off small steps helps many people see their progress.

quiz.say: Tidying your room feels too big. What can you do?
quiz.show: Your room feels too big to tidy. What helps?

options.show: Do it all at once very fast
options.say: Do it all at once very fast

quiz.why: Small steps, like toys first, make a big job feel easy.

wrong.1: You can do it. Small steps make it possible.
wrong.2: All at once feels heavy. One step at a time is calmer.

quiz.say: What is a good first step for tidying?
quiz.why: Just the toys is one small, clear job you can start right now.

wrong.1: The whole room is the big job. Cut it smaller.
wrong.2: That is even bigger. Start with one small thing.
